property_summary: For any caller, after a call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, if the caller is not an admin, winnersPerPeriod must remain unchanged; the mutant allows any caller to change it, so a non-admin can alter it.
For any caller that is not an admin, calling updateWinnersPerPeriod must not change winnersPerPeriod; the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
For any non-admin caller, invoking updateWinnersPerPeriod must not change the value of winnersPerPeriod; the mutant allows any caller to change it.
For any caller that is not an admin, a call to updateWinnersPerPeriod should revert; the mutant omits the admin check, so a non-admin call succeeds and changes winnersPerPeriod.

After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, the value of winnersPerPeriod must equal the argument passed; the mutant does not update it, so after a call with a non-zero argument, winnersPerPeriod remains its previous value.

After a call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by an admin, at least one observable state change occurs (e.g., winnersPerPeriod changes) if the new value differs from the current one; the mutant never updates the variable, so a subsequent read of winnersPerPeriod always returns its initial value regardless of the argument.
After a successful call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by an admin, the value of winnersPerPeriod must equal the passed argument; the mutant leaves it unchanged.

For any non-zero argument passed by an admin, calling updateWinnersPerPeriod must change winnersPerPeriod to that argument; the mutant never updates the variable, so an admin call followed by a non-admin call to pickWinner (which reads winnersPerPeriod) reveals the unchanged value.
After an admin calls updateWinnersPerPeriod, the value of winnersPerPeriod must be equal to the argument passed; the mutant never updates the variable, so winnersPerPeriod remains unchanged.
After an admin calls updateWinnersPerPeriod, the stored winnersPerPeriod MUST equal the argument passed; the mutant always sets it to 1, violating this when newWinnersPerPeriodAmount != 1.

For any admin call to updateWinnersPerPeriod with any argument, the resulting winnersPerPeriod MUST equal the argument; the mutant breaks this because it always sets winnersPerPeriod to 1 regardless of the input.

For any admin call to updateWinnersPerPeriod with any argument, the resulting winnersPerPeriod MUST equal the argument; the mutant breaks this because it always sets winnersPerPeriod to 1 regardless of the input.

For any admin call to updateWinnersPerPeriod with a positive argument, the resulting winnersPerPeriod must be a positive value that enables the round selection process; the mutant always sets it to 1, and when the argument is 0, the reference sets it to 0 while the mutant sets it to 1, allowing the mutant to bypass the 'Incorrect number of winners' check in pickWinner.

After an admin updates winnersPerPeriod via updateWinnersPerPeriod, the resulting winnersPerPeriod must equal the argument passed; the mutant always sets it to 1, so pickWinner will revert for any winners array length not equal to 1 if the argument was different.
After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod, the stored winnersPerPeriod must equal the input argument, but in the buggy version it is always incremented by 1.

For any admin-given newWinnersPerPeriodAmount, after updateWinnersPerPeriod is called, the stored winnersPerPeriod must exactly match the provided argument; the bugged mutant adds 1, violating this equality.
After an admin calls updateWinnersPerPeriod, the value of winnersPerPeriod must exactly equal the provided newWinnersPerPeriodAmount; the mutant adds 1, so the two diverge.
For any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by an admin, the resulting winnersPerPeriod must equal the passed argument; the buggy mutant adds 1, violating this equality.
After updateWinnersPerPeriod is called by an admin, the stored winnersPerPeriod must be exactly the provided argument; the buggy mutant adds 1, so the equality fails.

The `winnersPerPeriod` state variable can only be updated by the owner, not by admins, after the bug change; the reference allows any admin to update it, while the buggy version restricts it to the owner.

After any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by a non-owner admin, the winnersPerPeriod value in the reference contract equals the new amount, but in the buggy contract it remains unchanged due to the stricter access control.

After a successful call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by any admin that is not the owner, the reference contract updates winnersPerPeriod to the passed amount, while the buggy contract leaves winnersPerPeriod unchanged.

For any call to updateWinnersPerPeriod by an account that is an admin but not the owner, the reference C updates winnersPerPeriod to the passed amount, while the buggy M leaves winnersPerPeriod unchanged.

For any allowed caller (admin) that is not the owner, updateWinnersPerPeriod succeeds and sets winnersPerPeriod to the given amount; the buggy version reverts when called by such an admin, so the new value never takes effect.
After any successful pickWinner call, roundId must increase by exactly 1, but the mutant increases it by 2, causing the next round's requirements to be checked against the wrong roundId.

After any number of pickWinner calls, the value of roundId must equal the number of completed selection rounds, but the mutant increments by 2 causing roundId to be larger than the count of rounds with isSelectionComplete set to true.

After any single successful pickWinner call, roundId must increase exactly by the number of distinct selection rounds completed (which is 1), but the mutant increases it by 2, so a subsequent call to pickWinner with the same roundId as the previous call is incorrectly allowed.

After any sequence of successful pickWinner calls, roundId must equal the number of rounds for which isSelectionComplete is true, but the mutant increases roundId twice per call, so the invariant roundId == count of completed rounds breaks.
After any number of successful pickWinner calls, roundId must equal the count of rounds for which isSelectionComplete is true, but the mutant increments by 2 per call, breaking this invariant.
After a successful pickWinner, roundId must strictly increase; the bug breaks this because it never increments roundId, so roundId stays stuck at 0.

After two successful pickWinner calls, the reference contract stores distinct winnerAddresses entries for round 0 and round 1, while the buggy version overwrites round 0's entry because roundId never increments.

After any number of successful pickWinner calls, the contract's roundId must equal the number of completed rounds (i.e., the count of true entries in isSelectionComplete); the bug violates this by never incrementing roundId.

After any call to pickWinner, if that call did not revert, the value of roundId must equal the number of completed non-empty rounds (which is the count of true entries in isSelectionComplete up to the current roundId); the bug violates this by failing to increment roundId, so it stays 0 while isSelectionComplete[0] may be true.

For any sequence of successful pickWinner calls, the number of distinct round IDs with a recorded winner must equal the number of pickWinner calls that did not revert; the bug violates this because it never increments roundId, causing subsequent calls to overwrite round ID 0.
After pickWinner executes, totalPoints must equal the sum of all fighterPoints across all IDs; the mutant violates this because it unconditionally sets totalPoints to 0.
